Peter,

Every morning I wake up, determined to get the most out of each day. I'm an optimist and firmly believe it takes more effort to have a bad day than a good one.

But I've got to tell you, MSNBC and their cast of far-Left characters do their best to ruin my day as often as they can. You might recall that earlier this year one of their regular panelists began attacking our Senate campaign.

In April, he called me an **"ignorant neophyte,"** and said that my candidacy is **"a white insult to Black people."**

Then he called Senator Tim Scott and me _**"tokens"**_ who are _**"shucking and jiving for their white handlers."** _

Now, he's back at it again, saying this about me on MSNBC earlier this week:

| _**"Walker is doing what he's told, and that is what Republicans like. That's what Republicans want from their negroes: to do what they're told."**_
---

I'll repeat what I said in April: **this is racist, disgusting, and sad.**

What's also disturbing is that our opponent, who also happens to be Black, has never once condemned any of these blatantly racist remarks. _Can you imagine if these comments were made by a conservative about a Black Democrat? The outrage would be instantaneous and overwhelming - and rightly so._

_**Senator Warnock's silence is deafening and disappointing.**_

clean_body: I’ll repeat what I said before: this is racist, disgusting, and sad. | Peter, Every morning I wake up, determined to get the most out of each day. I'm an optimist and firmly believe it takes more effort to have a bad day than a good one. But I've got to tell you, MSNBC and their cast of far-Left characters do their best to ruin my day as often as they can. You might recall that earlier this year one of their regular panelists began attacking our Senate campaign. In April, he called me an "ignorant neophyte," and said that my candidacy is "a white insult to Black people." Then he called Senator Tim Scott and me "tokens" who are "shucking and jiving for their white handlers." Now, he's back at it again, saying this about me on MSNBC earlier this week: | "Walker is doing what he's told, and that is what Republicans like. That's what Republicans want from their negroes: to do what they're told." I'll repeat what I said in April: this is racist, disgusting, and sad. What's also disturbing is that our opponent, who also happens to be Black, has never once condemned any of these blatantly racist remarks. Can you imagine if these comments were made by a conservative about a Black Democrat? The outrage would be instantaneous and overwhelming - and rightly so. body:
Too often politicians go to Washington and forget about the people they were elected to serve.
#

Too often politicians go to Washington and forget about the people they were elected to serve. They put their own interests first and start to think they’re above the law.
Get this, at least 64 members of Congress have broken a law to stop insider stock trading, yet most people in Washington refuse to do anything about it.
But I say we should ban members of Congress from trading stocks all together. Let’s put it to a vote and dare politicians like my opponent to vote against it.
[**If you agree, add your name today to tell Congress to ban their members from trading stocks. Our Senators should be working for you, not themselves.**](https://act.cheribeasley.com/signup/ban-stock-trading-pt-em/?source=em220803-2-ma&akid=1376%2E357359%2E3tjVxZ)
When we win this race, there will be no question that I’m voting to put the needs of North Carolina families first — not corporate interests and wealthy insiders.
I don’t care who it upsets — I will not hesitate to cast my vote to ban members of Congress from trading stocks. We deserve a Senator who will fight for us, and who understands her job is to serve others.
Thank you for adding your voice and demanding accountability in Washington.
\- Cheri

clean_body: Judicial Watch announced recently that it filed an amici curiae (friend of the court) brief along with the Allied Educational Foundation (AEF) in support of the Coalition for Thomas Jefferson High School’s challenge to race-based admissions policies for the nationally-known public high school that were put in place at in Fairfax County, Virginia | | | | | | Because no one is above the law! | August 03, 2022 ---|---|--- | | == == Judicial Watch announced recently that it filed an amici curiae (friend of the court) brief along with the Allied Educational Foundation (AEF) in support of the Coalition for Thomas Jefferson High School’s challenge to race-based admissions policies for the nationally-known public high school that were put in place at in Fairfax County, Virginia. == | | | Judicial Watch While American families struggle during record-high inflation and a looming recession, the Biden administration celebrates the launch of a government website dedicated to heat and loaded with costly federal resources. Specifically, the new site, heat.gov, aims to reduce the health risks of extreme heat by providing the public and decision-makers with timely information. Not surprisingly, the administration has assessed that minorities and the poor, as well as the “highly diverse” LGBTQIA+ communities, are disproportionately impacted by heat-related health issues and therefore it had that demographic in mind when launching the project. == Judicial Watch Though Congress has repeatedly denied laws to give needy families government-subsidized diapers—in addition to free medical care and food—the Biden administration is quietly allocating millions of dollars to the cause originally funded by the Obama administration to end a pandemic of “diaper disparity.” A Health and Human Services (HHS) division known as Administration for Children and Families (ACF) Office of Community Services (OCS) is doling out $8 million to provide diapers and diapering supplies through government distribution programs for families with low incomes. == Newsmax The Department of Defense has again drawn the ire of a prominent conservative watchdog group, amid accusations of teaching critical race theory at another military academy. Peter,

For the first time in Georgia's history, both Democrats and Republicans have nominated a Black man for the U.S. Senate.

This is indeed historic and speaks to the greatness of America's experiment with democracy. Less than 70 years ago, people like Senator Raphael Warnock and me were not able to attend the same schools as white children.

Now, we're running against one another - two Black men - in what is shaping up to be the most competitive Senate race of the entire 2022 midterm elections. Fox News has even gone so far as to say, _**"The U.S. Senate race in Georgia is key for determining control of the upper house next year."**_

**That may be where the similarities end.**

If you've read recent emails from my campaign, you'll recall that a far-Left columnist - and a regular guest on MSNBC - has trained his fire on me. Since April, he has lobbed multiple racial epithets against me that are offensive to me personally and to the entire Black community.

In the past, he said:

| _**"Herschel Walker's candidacy is a white insult to Black people."**_
---

and
_**"I make a hard distinction between black conservatives and these tokens (I.E. HERSCHEL WALKER AND TIM SCOTT), who are out here right now, shucking and jiving for their white handlers."**_
---

This week, he went on MSNBC and lobbed his most disgusting attack yet: _**"Walker is doing what he's told, and that is what Republicans like. That's what Republicans want from their Negroes: to do what they're told."**_
---

**Shame on him for saying it, and shame on MSNBC for airing it.**

Despite these racially based insults making national news, Senator Warnock has said nothing.

Unfortunately, Senator Warnock's silence is deafening.

It puzzles me that Senator Warnock has failed to condemn any of the overtly racist attacks or that he has failed to condemn MSNBC for giving this racial commentator a platform.

clean_body: Shame on him for saying it, and shame on MSNBC for airing it. | Peter, For the first time in Georgia's history, both Democrats and Republicans have nominated a Black man for the U.S. Senate. This is indeed historic and speaks to the greatness of America's experiment with democracy. Less than 70 years ago, people like Senator Raphael Warnock and me were not able to attend the same schools as white children. Now, we're running against one another - two Black men - in what is shaping up to be the most competitive Senate race of the entire 2022 midterm elections. Fox News has even gone so far as to say, "The U.S. Senate race in Georgia is key for determining control of the upper house next year." That may be where the similarities end. If you've read recent emails from my campaign, you'll recall that a far-Left columnist - and a regular guest on MSNBC - has trained his fire on me. Since April, he has lobbed multiple racial epithets against me that are offensive to me personally and to the entire Black community. In the past, he said: | "Herschel Walker's candidacy is a white insult to Black people." and "I make a hard distinction between black conservatives and these tokens (I.E. HERSCHEL WALKER AND TIM SCOTT), who are out here right now, shucking and jiving for their white handlers." This week, he went on MSNBC and lobbed his most disgusting attack yet: "Walker is doing what he's told, and that is what Republicans like. That's what Republicans want from their Negroes: to do what they're told." Shame on him for saying it, and shame on MSNBC for airing it. Despite these racially based insults making national news, Senator Warnock has said nothing. Unfortunately, Senator Warnock's silence is deafening. It puzzles me that Senator Warnock has failed to condemn any of the overtly racist attacks or that he has failed to condemn MSNBC for giving this racial commentator a platform. In fact, it also puzzles me why Senator Warnock continues to give interviews on MSNBC despite the racist attacks they air against me. Thank you for standing with me. From his days as an Illinois State Senator, to U.S. Senator, and later as President, Barack Obama _always_ focused on making government work better for working people.

_He's Illinois' own and we couldn't be more grateful for all he's done to better our state and nation._

**Last night, voters in Kansas dealt a major blow to anti-choice extremists when they voted to maintain protections for reproductive freedom.**
By a margin of over 20 points, Kansans refused to remove abortion rights from the state constitution. Right-wing activists threw everything they had at this effort, including disinformation texts to voters – but Kansans stood up and said _no_.
**We can do that here.** I’m supporting a similar amendment to the Ohio constitution to protect and defend the right to the full range of reproductive care, including abortion – because these decisions should be dictated by patients and their families, not politicians.
**[Abortion is on the ballot in Ohio this year. Which is exactly why we need to amend the Ohio constitution to restore reproductive rights and ensure that Ohioans aren’t forced to leave the state or forgo care altogether. The status quo is unacceptable. But we can change it.
